summary: Dotta introduces Paperclip, an open-source agent orchestrator for zero-human companies, which he describes as the human control plane for AI labor. Users create org charts of AI agents, set goals, automate jobs, and remain involved in the task process from design through execution. Onboarding is simple: run NPX Paperclip AI onboard with an optional --yes flag for defaults. A core principle is bring your own agent — Gemini, Claude, Codex, Hermes, Open Claw, and others can all be integrated as employees with shared memory and communication. Dotta demonstrates using his real Paperclip instance to manage the Paperclip project itself, showing a CEO, CTO, coders, and a marketing org. He highlights a practical example: after crossing 40,000 GitHub stars, he asked his CEO agent to hire a video writer, install the Remotion skill, and produce a branded celebration animation in about 5 minutes — work that might have taken a week. Paperclip features a built-in skills manager where agents find and install capabilities. For reliability, vendor-neutral QA agents using the agent browser skill and approver workflows ensure tasks meet instructions before completion. Routines enable scheduled or manual reusable tasks with template variables. Dotta emphasizes Paperclip is not a coding tool — it is designed for creating businesses and can be used for marketing, sales, finance, and engineering by technical and non-technical users alike. He demonstrates creating a new company live, starting with a CEO agent that requests hiring a CTO, which Dotta approves. He advises starting with only needed agents rather than importing large templates, configuring instructions carefully, and using cheaper models via Open Router for less demanding work. Paperclip tracks monthly spend with per-agent and per-project budgets. A meta-agent called a skill consultant helps other agents use skills effectively. The current version is early; organizational learning is largely manual but will be automated. The roadmap includes workspaces, CEO chat, maximizer mode, multi-user support, cloud and sandboxed agent deployments, a free desktop app, and improved memory and knowledge base. During the talk, Paperclip crossed 50,000 GitHub stars. Dotta closes by encouraging viewers to visit paperclip.ing and start using Paperclip today, emphasizing it is free and gives humans control over AI labor.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduces Paperclip
sections.summary: Dotta introduces Paperclip as an open-source agent orchestrator for zero-human companies, describing it as the human control plane for AI labor. Users set up org charts of agents, manage them, invoke their taste, and have them complete real work while remaining involved in the task process.

sections.title: Getting Started
sections.summary: Onboarding via NPX Paperclip AI onboard with optional --yes flag. Dotta demonstrates his real Paperclip instance managing the Paperclip project with CEO, CTO, coders (Codex and Claude), and marketing org. Key principle: bring your own agent — Gemini, Claude, Codex, Hermes, Open Claw all supported as employees with shared memory and communication.

sections.title: Skill Management
sections.summary: Every part of Paperclip has an agentic surface. CEO agents can hire new agents and install skills via the built-in skills manager. Demonstrated by creating a Remotion video celebrating 40,000 GitHub stars — CEO hired a video writer, installed Remotion best practices skill, created a plan, and after feedback produced a branded animation in ~5 minutes. Skills can be improved over time by learning from agent feedback to create org-specific skills with branding and pacing preferences.

sections.title: Reliable Workflows
sections.summary: Paperclip provides vendor-neutral workflows for reliability. QA agents use the agent browser skill to test work. Tasks can require reviewers and approvers — QA iterates with the coder while the manager approves. Solves the common problem of agents skipping instructions like browser testing before returning work.

sections.title: Routine Automation
sections.summary: Routines enable scheduled or manual reusable tasks with template variables, such as creating Discord messages for merged PRs or writing release changelogs. Routines can be grouped by project or agent and overlap with skills. Paperclip uses Greptile for first-pass code reviews of community contributions.

sections.title: Agentic Flexibility
sections.summary: Dotta emphasizes Paperclip is not a coding tool but a business creation tool usable for marketing, sales, finance, and more by non-technical users. He demonstrates creating a new company (Agent Tools Directory) live, starting with a CEO agent that requests hiring a CTO, which Dotta approves. He advises starting small with only needed agents rather than importing large org templates, and using cheaper models via Open Router (e.g., Qwen 3.6 plus for free) for less demanding work while reserving frontier models for high-intelligence tasks. Paperclip tracks monthly spend with per-agent and per-project budgets and supports configurable concurrency (default one parallel agent).

sections.title: Future Roadmap
sections.summary: Dotta shows the importance of configuring agent instructions iteratively, demonstrating a Codex coder with evolving instructions and a skill consultant meta-agent that diagnoses agents not using skills properly. The current version is early with manual organizational learning to be automated later. Roadmap includes workspaces, CEO chat, maximizer mode, multi-user support, cloud and sandboxed agent deployments (E2B, dev.exe), a free open-source desktop app, and improved memory and knowledge base. Paperclip crossed 50,000 GitHub stars live during the talk. Dotta closes by encouraging viewers to visit paperclip.ing and start using the free tool to control AI labor.
